A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCALE study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-E. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original coding experiments, human-intervention comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and case studies in Section 5 and Appendices C and E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the accuracy comparisons in Tables 2-5 and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: SCALE retains the same coder simulation, independent annotation, inter-agent discussion, codebook evolution, and human-intervention procedures. Appendix D.1 revises persona configurations within these existing components.

E1.justification: Table 1 and Appendix B.1 retain the same five datasets and seven classification tasks covering brand dialogue, cancer narratives and support, water-crisis emotions, and product-incident sentiment.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 retain GPT-4O and GPT-4O-mini with vanilla, chain-of-thought, tree-of-thought, and self-consistency prompting. Tables 3 and 5 retain the same intervention comparison sets.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 changes Sarah from a doctoral student to a researcher and rewrites Kenji from a computer-science graduate student specializing in NLP to an anthropology Ph.D. specializing in digital ethnography. These revise the reported agent configurations without establishing reruns. Model versions, metrics, and default N=2, B=20, K=3 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The discussion ablations, parameter sensitivity analyses in Figures 3 and 6, discussion analyses in Figures 4 and 7, and agreement, disagreement, and codebook case studies in Appendix E are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten independent runs and averaged results in Section 5.2. Run-count, seed, uncertainty, and significance-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2-5 retain their numerical entries, Figures 3, 4, 6, and 7 retain their results, and Appendix E retains its case outcomes. The persona revisions are not accompanied by new or revised reported results.

T1.justification: The mathematical workflow descriptions in Sections 3-4 and agreement-rate definitions in Appendix B.2 are unchanged. No theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about simulating content analysis, incorporating human intervention, improving scalability, and approximating human judgment. Contribution scope and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the interpretations of discussion benefits and impasses, difficulties restructuring codebook categories, and limitations involving bias, computational overhead, and dependence on human expertise.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GitHub code-access footnote on page 1 and revises the exact persona specifications in Appendix D.1. Other model identifiers, hyperparameters, and operational prompts are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and research positioning are unchanged. Removing the repeated Weber (1990) citation from the coding-definition footnote does not remove that work from the paper.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and heading edits, abbreviates one affiliation, rewrites a persona paragraph, and adds acknowledgments. The main narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 5 revise wording and labels. Figures 3 and 6 change colors, selected tick labels, and axis-title wording while preserving the plotted results. Added text causes limited reference and appendix reflow.

improvement.justification: The new code-access information and localized wording and figure-label corrections modestly improve documentation and usability. The empirical evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged. Revised personas are not linked to rerun results, so the revision does not establish stronger experimental validation.
